title: EWMA + Packet-loss weighted region arbiter for latency-tier routing with variant fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current region selection uses raw p50/p95 latency windows which reacts noisily to transient spikes and ignores network quality signals (packet loss / retransmit). Consequence: user requests sometimes route to regions with low median latency but high loss, increasing tail latency and token cost due to retries and TCP backoff. Goal: build an arbiter that combines latency percentiles and network health into a single score, applies EWMA decay to smooth short bursts, and tier-aware routing so Dedicated/Hosted/Private capacity is respected. Also wire in fallback to model variants (quantized / lower-memory) when region-level capacity or health degrades.

Approach (summary):
1) Compute per-region metrics on a 10s window then push into an EWMA with two time constants (fast=30s, slow=10m) for p50 and p95 and for network loss and retransmit rate.
2) Normalize metrics into unitless penalties: latency penalty (p50/p95 buckets), loss penalty (packets lost per 1k), and retransmit penalty. Loss penalty increases non-linearly above 0.5%.
3) Weighted composite score = w1 * norm_p95 + w2 * norm_p50 + w3 * norm_loss + w4 * norm_retransmit + tier_penalty + variant_capacity_penalty. Default weights: w1=0.45, w2=0.25, w3=0.20, w4=0.10.
4) Hysteresis & grace: require composite score to be worse than best-by >10% for 3 consecutive EWMA samples before switching; allow forced immediate switch for safety circuit-breaker events (loss>5% or p95>2000ms).
5) Fallback model selection: maintain region -> compatible-variant ranking (e.g., fp16 -> int8-q4 -> int8-q3). If composite score is bad or capacity shortfall detected, prefer lower-cost variant but only if eval quality delta < configured threshold (default 1.5% perplexity or model-level eval metric).

Constraints & tradeoffs:
- Smoothing reduces flip-flopping but delays reaction to real outages; we mitigate with circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Weighting favors p95 to protect tails at cost of some median degradation.
- Variant fallback trades quality for availability; must be gated by evals and manual opt-outs for enterprise tenants.

Operational metrics to track:
- Route-change rate (changes/min) per POP and global
- % requests routed to non-primary region due to composite score
- QoS deltas after fallback (latency, token cost, model-quality regression)
- False-switch incidents (switches where post-switch score still worse)

Experiment plan:
- Week 1 (canary): deploy arbiter in read-only mode to shadow decisions and log what would have been chosen vs current router. Collect 72h of traffic across four high-volume POPs.
- Week 2 (A/B): enable arbiter for 10% traffic with rollback on increased error rates or customer impact.
- Week 3: expand to >50% with staged rollouts and selected enterprise opt-ins.

Success criteria:
- 10% reduction in tail latency (p95) on canaried POPs without more than 2% increase in p50 globally.
- No model-quality regression >1.5% on production eval suite due to variant fallbacks.
- Route-change rate < 2 changes/min per POP on average after hysteresis stabilizes.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow mode logs match expected composite scoring for 95% of sampled intervals
Canary A/B shows <=1% increase in total errors and >=8% p95 improvement in target POPs
Fallback variant selection has automated guardrails: eval delta check + per-customer opt-out
Grafana dashboard panels for composite score, contribution breakdown, and route-change rate are live
risks: Smoothing window set incorrectly causes slow reaction to real outages
Weight vector tuned for current traffic could be suboptimal for other regions or large-prod traffic patterns
Fallback variants may introduce customer-visible quality regressions if evals are not representative
Metric cardinality blowup in telemetry if we track too many per-POP/per-model combos
